reconcile.note: Clarke reads Ezra's "son of Iddo" as grandson, since Zechariah's own opening verse names Berechiah as the intervening father.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Zechariah is called son of Barachias in Zechariah 1:1 yet, via Targumic confusion, a grandson of Iddo, the same slippage behind Ezra's 'son of Iddo'.

quotes.text: the prophet Zechariah, who was a son of Barachias…especially as a Targum, evidently in consequence of a like confusion with the prophet who was a grandson of Iddo, calls the murdered Zechariah a son of Iddo.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), on Zechariah 1:1 and Ezra 5:1.

sides.snippet: Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem
sides.verseText: Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem; in the name of the God of Israel [prophesied they] to them.

sides.snippet: the word of Yahweh came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet
sides.verseText: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of Yahweh came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying,
